intro: A sensor summary should reflect reliability weights without treating a weight as another measured feature.
task: Return a dictionary with weighted mean and population variance for a one-dimensional measurement vector.
requirements: x and weights are nonempty finite vectors of equal length. Weights are nonnegative and their sum is positive.
Normalize by total weight for both mean and variance; this is population variance, with no sample correction.
Return Python numeric scalars under keys mean and variance. Zero-weight observations contribute nothing.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Divide weights by their sum before taking the dot product with measurements.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: A single positive weight gives zero variance even when other observations are far away.

explanation: Weights define how much each observation contributes to the summary. Normalizing by their sum makes a weight of two mean twice the influence, regardless of the overall scale.
Compute the mean first, then the weighted average of squared deviations. Centering before squaring also avoids subtracting two large nearly equal second moments.
Try multiplying every weight by ten. The summary must stay fixed. Then give an extreme observation zero weight and explain why it should have no effect.
formula: μ = Σwᵢxᵢ / Σwᵢ; variance = Σwᵢ(xᵢ − μ)² / Σwᵢ
